x: PVC is made from vinyl chloride, polythene from ethene, polystyrene from styrene and Teflon from tetrafluoroethene, giving a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii.
t: Recall the monomer of each polymer.

x: Buna-S comes from 1,3-butadiene and styrene (S for styrene). Butadiene with acrylonitrile gives Buna-N.
t: Discriminate Buna-S (styrene) from Buna-N (nitrile).

x: Both are true and R explains A: thermoplastics soften on heating and set on cooling again and again, so they can be remoulded and recycled.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Option B is incorrect: Terylene is made from two monomers (ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid), so it is a copolymer, not a homopolymer. The other descriptions are right.
t: Count the monomers to tell homopolymer from copolymer.

x: I, III and IV are correct: proteins, nucleic acids and natural rubber are natural polymers. II is false because rayon is semi-synthetic, made from cellulose.
t: Discriminate natural, semi-synthetic and synthetic polymers.

x: Teflon is used in non-stick pans, Bakelite in switches and plugs, Buna-S in tyres and Glyptal in paints and lacquers, giving a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall the use of each polymer.

x: Both are true and R explains A: microbes break biodegradable polymers down, so they do not pile up in the environment.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Nylon-2-Nylon-6 is made from glycine and aminocaproic acid and is biodegradable. Nylon-6,6 uses hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid.
t: Recall the monomers of each nylon.

x: Statement A is true: vulcanised rubber is natural rubber modified with sulphur, so it is semi-synthetic. Statement B is false because silk is a natural protein polymer.
t: Discriminate natural from semi-synthetic polymers.

x: Three are biodegradable: PHBV, starch and proteins. PVC is a non-biodegradable synthetic plastic.
t: Recall the biodegradable polymers.

x: Polypropene comes from propene, natural rubber from isoprene, neoprene from chloroprene and nylon-6,6 from hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the monomer of each polymer.

x: All three are correct: PVC and Teflon are each made by addition from a single monomer, and both are thermoplastics.
t: Recall the class of each polymer.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the cis-polyisoprene structure describes what rubber is, not why it is formed by addition or behaves as an elastomer.
t: Check whether R is a reason or only a structure.

x: All three are correct: starch and cellulose are glucose polymers, wool is a natural protein polymer, and DNA and RNA are nucleic acids.
t: Recall the natural polymers.

x: Both are true: rayon includes cellulose acetate, and cellulose nitrate (gun cotton) is a semi-synthetic polymer.
t: Recall the semi-synthetic polymers.

x: Polythene is a homopolymer, made only from ethene units. It is an addition polymer, not cross-linked or condensation.
t: Count the monomers in the polymer.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Buna-S is a copolymer because it has two monomers; being elastic is a separate property.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: PHBV is made from 3-hydroxybutanoic acid and 3-hydroxypentanoic acid and is biodegradable. Terylene, nylon-6,6 and nylon-2-nylon-6 use the other pairs.
t: Recall the monomers of PHBV.

x: All eight are synthetic: polythene, PVC, nylon, Terylene, Bakelite, Teflon, Buna-S and neoprene are made entirely in factories.
t: Recall the synthetic polymers.

x: All six are thermoplastics: polythene, PVC, polystyrene, polypropene, Teflon and nylon can be softened and reshaped by heat.
t: Discriminate thermoplastics from thermosets.

x: Both are true and R explains A: heating forms permanent cross-links between chains, which sets the polymer hard.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Both are true: thermosets cannot be remoulded once cross-linked, and Bakelite is a classic thermoset.
t: Discriminate thermosets from thermoplastics.

x: All three are thermosets: melamine-formaldehyde, urea-formaldehyde and Glyptal all form cross-linked networks.
t: Recall the thermosetting polymers.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: HDPE's linear, closely packed chains cause both its higher melting point and its strength.
t: Check whether R is a cause or a parallel effect.

x: Both are true: PVC can be rigid or flexible and insulates and resists chemicals, and Teflon resists heat and chemicals.
t: Recall the properties of PVC and Teflon.

x: Nylon is strong, elastic and abrasion-resistant, Terylene strong, crease-resistant and quick-drying, Bakelite hard and insulating, and rubber elastic, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.
t: Recall the key property of each polymer.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: neoprene's oil resistance has nothing to do with sulphur vulcanising natural rubber.
t: Check whether R is about the same material as A.

x: All four are polythene uses: bags, bottles, toys and pipes.
t: Recall the uses of polythene.

x: Polypropene is used for ropes and carpets, PVC for pipes and raincoats, polystyrene for packaging and cabinets, and Teflon for gaskets and seals, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the use of each polymer.

x: Both are true: polythene is used for electrical insulation and for packaging.
t: Recall the uses of polythene.

x: All five are correct: both nylon-6 and nylon-6,6 make fibres and ropes, and nylon-6,6 also makes tyre cords.
t: Recall the uses of nylons.

x: LDPE is soft, flexible and low-density, while HDPE is tough, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Discriminate LDPE from HDPE.

x: Nylon-6 is used for tyre cords and carpets, and nylon-6,6 for carpets and textiles. Since List-II only numbers the uses, the code pairs them in order, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall that the code pairs items in order when List-II repeats.

x: Nylon-6 is used for textiles and gears, nylon-6,6 for gears and Terylene for fabrics. With "Gears" repeated, the code pairs in order, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall that the code pairs items in order when List-II repeats.

x: All three are correct: PET (Terylene) is used for bottles, films and polyester clothing.
t: Recall the uses of PET.

x: All five are correct: Bakelite is used for handles, combs and laminates, and melamine-formaldehyde for unbreakable crockery and laminates.
t: Recall the uses of thermosets.

x: All five are correct: neoprene makes conveyor belts, gaskets and oil-resistant hoses, and natural rubber makes tyres and footwear.
t: Recall the uses of rubbers.

x: Natural rubber makes gloves and balloons, vulcanised rubber makes tyres and biodegradable polymers make orthopaedic devices, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Recall the uses of rubbers and biopolymers.

x: All four are biodegradable: nylon-2-nylon-6, polylactic acid, polyglycolic acid and cellulose.
t: Recall the biodegradable polymers.

x: Both are true: biodegradable polymers are used in orthopaedic implants and for controlled drug release, since the body breaks them down.
t: Recall the medical uses of biopolymers.

x: All four are correct: polythene, polystyrene, nylon and Teflon are synthetic plastics that do not biodegrade.
t: Recall the non-biodegradable plastics.

x: All five are impacts of non-biodegradable plastics: persistence, pollution, microplastics, landfill problems and harm to wildlife.
t: Recall the effects of plastic pollution.

x: Both are true and R explains A: starch-blended plastics break down only partly, which is why they are called semi-biodegradable.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Biodegradable polymers are used in packaging that breaks down after use. Tyres use Buna-S, switches Bakelite and paints Glyptal.
t: Recall the uses of biopolymers.
